headline: DOWNSPOUT
ON YOUR *PATIO?*
beats.vo: Downspout dumping on your patio? That's a common reason pavers sink.

headline: KEEP IT *OFF*
YOUR PATIO
beats.vo: That water feeds the problems that *sink pavers*, *push walls* and *rot fence posts*.

headline: SLOPE IT *AWAY*
FROM THE HOUSE
beats.vo: The ground should fall *away* from your house. Patios and walks typically slope about *two percent*.

headline: ROUTE IT TO AN
*APPROVED* DRAIN
beats.vo: Route roof water into the *approved drainage* for your lot and your city.

headline: NOVEMBER:
USUALLY *WETTEST*
beats.vo: *November* is usually our wettest month. Next big rain, go watch where the water goes.

beats.note: aligned low in the photo so the pickup truck parked above the wall stays out of the band

post.caption: Is your downspout dumping onto your patio this Metro Vancouver rainy season? Roof water aimed at a patio or behind a retaining wall is a common reason pavers sink and walls push out. Grade the ground away from the house and route downspouts into the approved drainage for your lot.
post.alt: A backyard paver patio beside a river-rock bed and the back of a house, an animated diagram of a downspout and ground sloping away from a house, a slab patio with a channel drain, and a wet paver walkway.
